beats.body:
Five names keep coming up. Put them in a proper table — no notebook scribbles.
We talk to databases in **SQL**. Let's start.

Every column has a **data type**. These are used often:

| Data type | Syntax |
|---|---|
| Integer | INTEGER / INT |
| Float | FLOAT |
| String | VARCHAR |
| Text | TEXT |
| Date | DATE |
| Time | TIME |
| Datetime | DATETIME |
| Boolean | BOOLEAN |

Notes: Boolean values are stored as integers **0 (FALSE)** and **1 (TRUE)**.
A date looks like `'YYYY-MM-DD'`. A datetime looks like `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'`.

beats.prompt: Pick the best data type for each piece of case information.

beats.body:
`CREATE TABLE` creates a new table in the database.
```sql
CREATE TABLE table_name (
  column1 type1,
  column2 type2,
  ...
);
```

`INSERT INTO` adds rows to a table. You can add many rows in one query:
```sql
INSERT INTO table_name (column1, column2, ...)
VALUES

  (value1, value2, ...);
```

The `WHERE` clause keeps only the rows that satisfy a condition.
```sql
SELECT * FROM table_name WHERE condition;
```

`UPDATE` changes data that is already in a table.
```sql
UPDATE table_name SET c1 = value1;                    -- changes ALL rows
UPDATE table_name SET c1 = value1 WHERE condition;    -- changes only matching rows
```
